title: West Pakistan Labour Welfare Statistics Rule 1963

sections.shortTitle: West Pakistan Labour Welfare Statistics Rule 1963
sections.section: RULE - As In force in Punjab
sections.description:
LABOUR WELFARE STATISTICS (WEST PAKISTAN) RULES, 1963 [Gaz
LABOUR WELFARE STATISTICS (WEST PAKISTAN) RULES, 1963
[Gaz. of West Pak. Extr. 5 August 1963, p.
3637.]
[AS IN FORCE 1N THE PUNJAB]
[No. 5‑3 (L‑II)/63,
the 28th August 1963. Rules framed by West Pakistan Government in
exercise of the powers conferred by section 12 read with section 5 of the
Industrial Statistics Act, 1942, a draft of which was published In the Gazette
of West Pakistan. dated the 15th April 1963, under notification No.
3‑3 (L-II)/53, dated the 9th April 1963.]
1. Short title and commencement.‑--- (1) These rules may be
called the Labour Welfare Statistics (West Pakistan) Rules, 1963.
(2) They shall
come into force at once.
2. Definitions.‑--- (1) In these rules, unless there is
anything repugnant in the subject or context, the following expressions shall
have the meanings hereby respectively assigned to them, that is to say‑
(a) Act means the Industrial Statistics Act,
1942;
(b) Form means a form appended to these rules;
(c) Statistics Authority
means the authority appointed as such under section 4 of the Act.
(2) Any expression used in these
rules but not herein defined shall have the same meaning as in the Factories
Act, 1934 (XXV of 1934).
3. Service of notice by Statistics Authority.‑--- (1) The
notice to be served by or on behalf of the Statistics Authority under section 5
of the Act, shall be in Form A .
(2) A notice
meant for a Corporation may be served on the Secretary, or any Director, or
other principal officer of the Corporation, or by addressing it to the
Corporation at its registered office, and if it bas no registered office, then
at the principal place where the Corporation carries on its business.
(3) A notice
meant for a firm may be served upon any one or more of the partners‑or
upon any person having control or management of the partnership business at the
principal place at which the partnership business is carried on, and such
service shall be deemed good service upon the firm, whether all or any of the
partners are residing within or without the Province of West Pakistan.
(4) A notice
under these rules may be served by registered post acknowledgment due.
4. Submission of Returns.‑- (1) Every Occupier of a Factory
on whom a notice has been served under rule 3, shall furnish to the Statistics
Authority the following returns * * * on or before the date specified in
respect of each return
(a) A quarterly return * * * * Form B for
each quarter ending 31st March, 30th June, 30th September and 31st
Decem ber on or before the 15th of the month, following the quarter
to which the return relates.
(b) An annual return * * * * [The words in duplicate deleted. Noti. 5‑13
(Lab‑II)72 of 8 August 1973, Pb Gaz. Extr. 24 Aug.. 1973, p. 1261.]
in Form C on or before the 31st of January, following the year to
which it relates.
(2) Where a
factory has worked for a part of the year or a part of a quarter only, the
return shall relate to such part only.
(3) The returns
shall be posted to the Statistics Authority, Registered Acknowledgment due, in
a closed cover marked Confidential Labour Statistics Return .
5. Extension of time for the submission of Return.‑-- The
Statistics Authority may in any special case, for reasons to be recorded in
writing, extend the period for submission of an annual Return upto 60 days.
6. Manner for the submission of Returns.‑--- The returns to
be furnished under rule 4 shall conform to the directions set forth in Appendix
II, in the case of quarterly returns and ins Appendix II, in the case of annual
returns.
7. Relationship to other Rules under industrial Statistics Act, 1942.---
The returns to be furnished under these rules shall be in addition to the
returns to be furnished under the Industrial Statistics (West Pakistan) Rules,
1960.

sections.punishment:
punishable under section 8 of
the Industrial Statistics Act, 1942 which provides for a penalty which may
extend to 500 rupees or in case of continuing offence to 200 rupees for each
day during which the offence continues.
